scheme_name: National Mission on Edible Oil- Oil Palm: Replanting of Old Oil Palm Garden
description:
The National Mission on Edible Oil - Oil Palm is a significant initiative launched by the Government of India in 2014. 

This mission was introduced to reduce the country's dependence on imported edible oils. 

India is one of the largest consumers of edible oils globally, with a consumption of approximately 23 million metric tons in 2020. 

The mission aims to increase domestic production of edible oils, particularly palm oil, which has a higher yield compared to other oilseeds. 

The initiative is part of the broader goal to achieve self-sufficiency in edible oil production by 2025. 

The specific objective of the replanting of old oil palm gardens is to enhance productivity and sustainability. 

Old oil palm gardens, which are over 25 years old, often yield lower quantities of oil. 

The replanting initiative seeks to replace these old trees with high-yielding varieties. 

The targeted increase in productivity is expected to be around 3 to 4 tons of crude palm oil per hectare annually. 

The scheme aims to cover approximately 1 million hectares under oil palm cultivation by 2025. 

The estimated investment for the National Mission on Edible Oil - Oil Palm is around INR 11,040 crores over a period of five years. 

The replanting program is expected to create significant employment opportunities in rural areas. 

It is estimated that around 3 lakh jobs will be generated through this initiative. 

The benefits of the scheme include financial assistance to farmers for replanting activities. 

Farmers can receive up to INR 30,000 per hectare as a one-time assistance for replanting old oil palm gardens. 

This financial support is aimed at encouraging farmers to adopt modern agricultural practices. 

The eligibility criteria for farmers to avail of this assistance include being a registered oil palm grower. 

Farmers must also have a minimum landholding of 2 hectares to qualify for the replanting assistance. 

The age of the existing oil palm trees must be verified to ensure they are eligible for replanting. 

The application process for the replanting scheme involves several steps. 

Farmers must first register with the local agricultural department. 

They need to submit an application form along with documents proving their identity and land ownership. 

A verification process follows where officials assess the age and condition of the existing oil palm garden. 

Once approved, farmers receive the financial assistance directly into their bank accounts. 

The disbursement of funds occurs in a phased manner based on the progress of the replanting activities. 

The first installment is released upon approval, while subsequent installments are linked to the completion of specific milestones. 

The timeline for the replanting initiative is structured to ensure that farmers can complete the process within a stipulated period. 

The entire replanting process is expected to be completed within two years from the date of approval. 

The implementing authority for this mission is the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

The National Mission on Edible Oil - Oil Palm is coordinated by the Oil Palm Development Program under this ministry. 

State governments play a crucial role in the implementation of the scheme at the grassroots level. 

They are responsible for the identification of eligible farmers and the monitoring of the replanting process. 

The mission also focuses on research and development to improve oil palm varieties. 

The Indian Council of Agricultural Research is involved in developing high-yielding and disease-resistant oil palm varieties. 

The mission has set a target of achieving 10 million metric tons of palm oil production by 2025. 

This is expected to significantly reduce the import bill for edible oils, which was around INR 1.1 lakh crores in 2020. 

The government aims to increase the share of palm oil in the total edible oil consumption from the current 10% to 30% by 2025. 

The initiative also emphasizes sustainable farming practices to minimize environmental impact. 

Farmers are encouraged to adopt integrated pest management and organic farming techniques. 

The mission aligns with the government's vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

It is also expected to contribute to the overall economic development of rural areas. 

The replanting of old oil palm gardens is a crucial step towards achieving these objectives. 

The government has also initiated awareness programs to educate farmers about the benefits of oil palm cultivation. 

Workshops and training sessions are conducted to provide technical knowledge and support. 

The mission is supported by various financial institutions that provide loans to farmers for oil palm cultivation. 

The government has also introduced a subsidy scheme to make the cultivation of oil palm more attractive. 

This subsidy covers the cost of planting materials and technical assistance. 

The Oil Palm Development Program has been implemented in several states including Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Tamil Nadu. 

These states have been identified for their suitable climatic conditions for oil palm cultivation. 

The government is actively promoting oil palm cultivation in the northeastern states as well. 

The replanting of old oil palm gardens is a vital component of this strategy. 

The mission is expected to have a multiplier effect on the rural economy. 

It will enhance the livelihoods of farmers and create a sustainable source of income. 

The initiative is also aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals set by the United Nations. 

It aims to promote responsible consumption and production patterns. 

The National Mission on Edible Oil - Oil Palm is a comprehensive approach to address the challenges of edible oil production in India. 

It focuses on increasing domestic production while ensuring environmental sustainability. 

The replanting of old oil palm gardens is a critical step in achieving these goals. 

The mission is a testament to the government's commitment to enhancing agricultural productivity and farmer welfare. 

Through this initiative, India aims to become self-reliant in edible oil production. 

The replanting program is expected to play a significant role in achieving this vision. 

Farmers are encouraged to participate actively in this initiative for mutual benefit. 

The government continues to monitor and evaluate the progress of the mission regularly. 

This ensures that the objectives are met and the benefits reach the intended beneficiaries. 

The National Mission on Edible Oil - Oil Palm is a forward-looking initiative with far-reaching implications for the agricultural sector in India.
